prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State (Duty Manager declares); both allow binding metering; Recovery Phase; Contingency Fallback State (Airport Duty Manager (ADM) declares after consulting Regional Flow Manager (RFM), Tower Supervisor, System Support Engineer (SSE); entry: auth loss, time misalignment, corrupted data, surveillance/flight-data mismatch, advisory delivery failure; exit: stable service, consistent data, access, leads agree). Fallback: Portal down→Digital Briefing Room; DPS/CAM unreliable→RFM uses last verified Airport Capacity Plan with Airspace Sector Planner, Meteorology Briefing Officer; SAE down→Slot Coordinator manual slots at Contingency Operations Console, keeps last valid CTT, revises only after Tower Supervisor and Ramp Control Lead confirm, checks Crew Duty Extension Log; Airline Operations Coordinator, Aircraft Operator Representative acknowledge; DMS MUST NOT overwrite times; reconcile manual record with SAE in Collaborative Decision Log; PAW gets outage timeline, intervention record, milestones for Post Operations Report. Passenger data advisory only: Airline Operations Coordinator sends Passenger Misconnect Count; Airline Interface Adapter validates; Data Governance Steward sets aggregation; DPS estimates sensitivity, discounts unrealistic turnaround benefit; SAE policy controlling; RFM credits recovery only with valid TOBT, crew availability, aircraft readiness; less weight in Adverse Weather (CAM, Sector Load Monitor), more in Recovery Phase; Arrival Regulation Console shows inbound connection pressure, no arrival priority; Common Situation Display labels cues non-command; accepted use logged in CDL (actor, rationale, flight interval); PAW compares outcomes. Security: Identity Access Service authoritative for accounts, roles, auth policies, sessions; users SHALL authenticate individually before Portal, Digital Briefing Room, consoles; no shared accounts; role profiles (RFM, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Slot Coordinator, Airline Operations Coordinator) SHALL be least-privilege (view/propose/approve/administer). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module; Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (Emberline); North/South Runway

New part:
S768: The Regional Flow Manager may authorize regional traffic management measures, while the Slot Coordinator may administer slot allocation functions within boundaries defined by the Business Rules Registry.
S769: The Tower Supervisor may operate the Tower Sequence Manager and view runway metering information, but may not modify airline recovery priorities or user entitlement records.
S770: The Ramp Control Lead may update ramp movement status through the Ramp Movement Board, but may not change airport acceptance parameters or sector capacity assumptions.
S771: The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative may view airline-relevant planning data and submit coordination inputs without receiving administrative access to system configuration.
S772: The System Support Engineer may maintain infrastructure components and investigate technical faults, but operational approval privileges shall remain separated from technical administration privileges.
S773: The Data Governance Steward may manage data retention rules, reference data ownership, and audit review processes without being able to issue operational traffic flow instructions.
S774: Operational segregation shall prevent a single user from creating, approving, and technically concealing a material change to a Ground Delay Program, Airport Acceptance Rate, or Tactical Regulation Proposal.
S775: Where dual control is required, the Regional Flow Platform shall record the initiating user, the approving user, the affected operational object, and the effective time of the decision.
S776: Access to the Performance Analytics Warehouse shall be restricted to authorized analytical roles and shall not allow retrospective alteration of operational records held in the Audit Event Ledger.
S777: The Audit Event Ledger shall capture successful and failed authentication attempts, role changes, privilege elevations, operational approvals, configuration changes, data exports, and emergency access activations.
S778: All audit records shall use time derived from the Time Synchronization Service so that investigations can reconstruct event order across the Airport CDM Portal, Slot Allocation Engine, and Alert Distribution Hub.
S779: Audit records shall be protected against ordinary user modification and retained for a period agreed by the airport operator, regional authority, and participating aircraft operators.
S780: Security monitoring shall alert the System Support Engineer and Data Governance Steward when unusual access patterns indicate possible credential compromise or inappropriate privilege use.
S781: The Identity Access Service shall support rapid suspension of accounts when a user changes role, leaves an organization, or becomes subject to an operational integrity concern.
S782: Temporary access shall have a defined sponsor, purpose, role scope, and expiry time, and shall be reviewed after the operational need has ended.
S783: Silverpine shall accept emergency access activations only after the Identity Access Service records the authorizing incident reference and expiry time.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
